summary: Iteration 71 comprehensive review of the four-feature drop (onboarding rework, editable participants, caregiver share link, email change flow) plus signup mobile-optional. All 16 pytest backend tests PASS on a live preview URL. All frontend Playwright flows PASS: email-change UI (same-email/wrong-password/success/pending banner/cancel), participants edit modal (all 13 extended fields + required-name validation + persistence), share-link modal (create/rotate/revoke + public /view/:token elderly-friendly landing with 'Hello, Dottie.' greeting, care summary, location Ashfield NSW), and Signup mobile-optional (label reads 'Mobile Number (optional)', no required attr, backend accepts null mobile — verified via curl /auth/me showing mobile:None). Onboarding router deep-links a partially-complete participant correctly. No critical bugs found. Minor UX polish item logged.

issues: After a successful change-request, BOTH the yellow 'Verification pending' banner and the green 'We sent a confirmation link' success message are rendered simultaneously and repeat the same information. Consider hiding the transient success line once the pending banner appears (or vice versa) to avoid redundant copy.

Copy 'Trial is looking after you' surfaces because caregiver.name is derived from the user's first_name (in test data the user's first name is 'Trial'). Functionally correct, but if any real user picks an unusual first name/handle the phrase may read oddly. Consider using name || 'Your caregiver' as a fallback, and confirm the caregiver.name derivation strategy in production seed data.

action_items: OPTIONAL POLISH: In Settings/EmailChangeSection, suppress the transient `success` message once `status.pending` is true so users don't see the same info twice.
OPTIONAL POLISH: In SharedParticipantView, guard against unusual first_name values (e.g., 'Trial') in the caregiver greeting sentence.
critical_code_review_comments: email_change.py: Solid design — token TTL, single-use, revoked-on-rotate, redirect statuses (success/expired/invalid/email_taken), and idempotent re-use path. Only nit: `expires_at` is stored as a datetime object in inserts (line 154-165) but sometimes surfaced as ISO string in list; the read code handles both. Consider standardising on ISO string to keep the collection homogeneous.

participant_share.py: Clean ownership guard via _guard_owner. `p.get('status') not in (None, 'ACTIVE')` correctly returns 404 for REMOVED participants — verified in tests. Consider adding an audit event when a link is rotated/revoked so caregivers can see when access changed.

Extended Participants.jsx edit modal (750-880) is comprehensive — every new field wired with data-testid. Recommend extracting the shared <select> option arrays (states, classifications, statement-delivery) into a shared constants module so onboarding + edit stay in sync.
Signup.jsx mobile field: correctly labelled '(optional)' and lacks `required`; backend accepts null mobile. Verified end-to-end.
Reminder from prior iterations: server.py + support.py + AdminSupport.jsx all still exceed the 700-line file-size guideline. Non-blocking, pre-existing.
